clips.scene: A single, clean line of European soldiers standing shoulder to shoulder on a churned, overcast battlefield near Legnica, Poland, April 9, 1241 — ONE line only, not multiple messy clusters. HAZEL is walking INSIDE this line, IN THE GAPS BETWEEN the soldiers (in among the ranks, part of the formation's own depth), NOT behind it and NOT outside looking at it from a distance. Because she is standing among them facing the SAME direction they are (the open horizon where the threat will come from), the soldiers immediately beside her are seen in SIDE PROFILE, each actively gripping a kite shield in their forward arm held OUT IN FRONT of their body facing outward toward the horizon (a shield is never slung or worn on the back while standing in line — it is always held actively facing the direction of the threat), spear in the other hand, point leveled forward. Everyone in the line — her included — faces the same direction. Every visible soldier does constant, disciplined micro-movement: adjusting a shield grip, resetting a spear, shifting weight, checking a neighbor's gear, bracing — never idle, never aimless wandering. She is urgent, delivering her FULL line uninterrupted. The INSTANT she finishes speaking, a war horn suddenly sounds — she turns sharply toward the same direction the whole line is already facing, the view swinging past her own shoulder toward the horizon; the shot ENDS on her alarmed profile as she registers that something is there, before anything on the horizon is clearly visible yet (the reveal itself is the NEXT clip, not this one).
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (breathless, urgent, to lens, COMPLETE sentence, not cut off): "April, 1241. Europe is about to face the Mongols."
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, one camera angle throughout, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take. She is walking the entire time, moving along INSIDE the single line of soldiers (among them, in the gaps between files), never behind the line looking at backs, never outside/distant from it. Soldiers beside her are seen in profile with their shields clearly held forward/outward, never on their backs. She delivers her full line clearly and completely — do NOT cut off or interrupt her dialogue. The horn sounds right as she finishes the line (interrupting the moment/beat afterward, not her speech), and she turns sharply in reaction to it, in the SAME direction the whole line is already facing (not an arbitrary direction, not toward the soldiers' backs). End the shot on her alarmed/startled expression looking toward the horizon, NOT on a resolved view of the Mongol army — that reveal belongs to the next clip.
clips.sound: Wind, banners snapping, the creak/clink of soldiers adjusting gear and shifting stance, horses breathing nearby, distant murmur of the forming line, then a SUDDEN loud war horn right as she finishes speaking

clips.scene: Continuous from clip 1's exact moment and location: HAZEL is still facing the horizon, facing the lens. NO slow layered build — the full chaotic scale is visible essentially immediately: a vast, dust-churning mass of Mongol cavalry already in motion, arrows being nocked, banners whipping, individual riders and horses distinct within the chaos (varied poses, visible composite bows and lamellar armor, natural overlap and spacing — not a flat repeated silhouette, but full scale shown at once, not built to across the shot). Riding at the front of the mass, visually distinguished by finer armor and a personal banner, a commander figure is visible — she spots him partway through the shot. CRITICAL: every visible Mongol rider's shield or bow is held actively in a forward-facing grip, engaged with the direction of the charge — never slung or visible on a rider's back (same physical-plausibility rule as the European line: a carried weapon/shield is always held facing the direction of action, never worn on the back while actively fighting/charging).
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (breathless, reacting to the scale AND delivering real historical information in the same breath — urgent, not a calm narration): "That's not a raiding party. That's an army." [spots the commander figure riding at the front] "Grandsons of Genghis Khan lead it. They already burned Kiev to the ground before they ever crossed into Poland." [already turning her body toward camp/Henry's position as she finishes — bridges into clip 2]
clips.action: Single continuous unbroken shot, one camera angle throughout, no cuts, no scene changes, real-time continuous take. The full scale of the charging horde is visible from very early in the shot — do NOT build slowly from a small resolved group to a wide reveal; this is immediate chaos and scale, matched to her urgent delivery. By the end of the line she is already turning her body away from the horizon toward camp (motion that clip 2 continues, not a fresh static start). Do not render the cavalry as a flat, repeated, or synthetic-looking silhouette — individual riders and horses must read as distinct photographed subjects even amid the chaos (varied poses, realistic overlapping, natural spacing, not a copy-pasted texture).
clips.sound: The war horn's echo fading, then a rising rumble of thousands of hooves, distant Mongol horns answering, wind carrying dust

clips.scene: Opens continuing the exact turning motion clip 1B ended on (motion continuation, not a fresh static start) — HAZEL arrives at Duke Henry II the Pious, mounted on his horse, nobles and soldiers around him, facing the lens the whole time with Henry visible over her shoulder/beside her in the same frame (never a separate reverse shot of him alone).
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (arriving, still completing the turn/approach from 1B): "Duke Henry the Second. He's leading them." HAZEL (to Henry, still facing the lens): "How many are we fighting?" [Henry] (grim, eyes on the horizon, visible in her frame): "Enough." [beat — Mongol cavalry begins moving in the background, visible over his shoulder in her shot] [Henry] (shouted — this exact line and the cavalry motion behind him are the bridge into clip 3, not a fresh unrelated start): "Hold the line!"
clips.action: Henry looks to the horizon BEFORE he answers — the look precedes the line, not after. He raises his weapon and calls to his own line only after Mongol movement is already visible behind him in the same continuous take. Single continuous unbroken shot, no cuts. End the shot with his shout and the cavalry's motion still building, ready to be picked up and closed to full gallop at the very start of clip 3.
clips.sound: Wind, restless horses, low murmur of nobles, Henry's voice grim and commanding, distant horns beginning on the Mongol side
